title: Read-heavy product page slowing down
prompt: Your e-commerce product page receives 100x more reads than writes, and database CPU is climbing as you scale. The page shows product details, price, inventory, reviews, and recommendations — most of which rarely change. How would you reduce database load without compromising correctness for the things that do change (price, inventory)?

title: Cache invalidation across regions
prompt: You operate a product catalog with a global edge cache (CDN) and a regional cache layer (Redis) in front of your database. A merchant updates a product price. How do you propagate the change so that no user sees stale prices longer than 60 seconds, while keeping cache hit rates high under normal traffic?

title: Cache stampede after expiry
prompt: A heavily-used cache entry expires at midnight. Within milliseconds, hundreds of concurrent requests miss the cache and hit your database simultaneously, causing a CPU spike and timeouts. Walk through how you'd prevent this without making the cache itself a bottleneck.

title: Hot cache key causing one Redis node to melt
prompt: Your Redis cluster has 12 shards. One key — the homepage feature list — receives 40% of all reads, and that one shard is at 95% CPU while the others sit at 20%. How would you address the imbalance without rewriting the application?

title: Counting page views
prompt: You need to count page views per article and display the count in real time on the article page. Traffic is around 1,000 views/second. A naive 'UPDATE articles SET views = views + 1' approach is causing row-level lock contention. What approach would you use?

title: Vertical scaling has run out
prompt: Your monolithic API runs on a single beefy server. CPU is consistently at 80% during business hours and you've already moved to the largest instance size your cloud provider offers. The team is reluctant to break up the monolith. What are your immediate and longer-term options?

title: Black Friday traffic spike
prompt: You're 3 weeks from Black Friday. Your platform handles 1,000 RPS normally; analytics suggest you'll see 10x that spike for a 2-hour window. You need confidence the system will survive without over-provisioning year-round. Walk through how you'd prepare.

title: Choosing SQL vs NoSQL for a new service
prompt: You're building a service that stores user activity events for analytics. Each event has a small fixed schema, you'll write billions per day, and queries are mostly aggregations over time ranges. You read very rarely and never need joins to other data. Would you choose a relational or non-relational store, and why?

title: Multi-region read replicas with stale reads
prompt: Your primary database is in us-east. Read replicas in eu-west and ap-southeast serve regional users. Replication lag is usually under 1 second but occasionally spikes to 10 seconds during heavy writes. A user complains they updated their profile but it shows the old name on refresh. How do you handle this?

title: Sharding a 10TB user table
prompt: Your users table has grown to 10TB, queries are slow, and backups take 8 hours. You've decided to shard. Walk through how you'd choose a shard key, how you'd handle the migration with zero downtime, and what queries become hard after sharding.

title: Schema change on a 500GB table
prompt: You need to add a new non-null column to a 500GB Postgres table that's read and written constantly. Your downtime budget is zero. How would you approach this?

title: Hash passwords correctly
prompt: A junior dev wrote 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ? AND password = SHA256(?)' for login. Walk through everything wrong with this and what the right approach is.

title: API key leaked on GitHub
prompt: A contractor pushed a config file with your production database credentials to a public GitHub repo. You discovered it 4 hours later. Walk through the incident response.

title: Designing rate limiting that resists abuse
prompt: Your public API offers 1,000 requests/hour per API key on the free tier. A customer claims they're hitting the limit too quickly; investigation reveals they're sharing one key across 50 servers. Meanwhile another user has scripted 100 free accounts to bypass the limit entirely. How do you design rate limiting that handles both cases fairly?

title: Why use a message queue instead of HTTP calls?
prompt: When a user signs up, your service needs to: send a welcome email, create a Stripe customer, post to Slack, and add them to a CRM. Currently each one is a synchronous HTTP call from the signup handler. Sometimes signups time out because Slack's API is slow. What would you change?

title: Exactly-once delivery is impossible — now what?
prompt: Your billing service processes payment-completed events from a queue. The queue guarantees at-least-once delivery. A duplicate event must not double-charge the customer. Design the consumer side.

title: Out-of-order events in a stream
prompt: You're consuming user-activity events from Kafka with multiple partitions. Two events for the same user arrive on different partitions in the wrong order — the 'user logged out' event is processed before the 'user logged in' event. How would you handle ordering correctly without losing parallelism?

title: Health check is lying
prompt: Your service's /health endpoint returns 200 OK as long as the process is running. The load balancer routes traffic to 3 instances. One instance has lost connection to the database — every real request returns 500, but /health still returns 200, so the LB keeps sending traffic. What would you change?

title: Circuit breaker tripping in production
prompt: Your order-service depends on inventory-service. Inventory is slow today — 95th percentile latency is 8 seconds, up from 200ms. Order requests are piling up, threads are blocked, and the order-service is now unhealthy too. Walk through how to design protection against this kind of cascading failure.

title: Designing for 99.99% availability
prompt: Your customer is asking for a 99.99% uptime SLA — about 52 minutes of allowed downtime per year. You currently run on a single AWS region with no formal failover plan. Walk through what would need to change.

title: Adding logging that won't slow things down
prompt: Your service handles 5,000 requests per second. You want to log every request with timing and user info, but writing each log line to a remote log server adds 20ms of latency. How would you log without harming response time?

title: Picking the right metric to alert on
prompt: Your team has 50 alerts configured. Every week, half of them fire and the on-call ignores most of them as flaky. You're tasked with cleaning this up. How do you decide which alerts to keep, change, or delete?

title: Distributed trace shows 500ms gap
prompt: A user reports a page that takes 3 seconds to load. The distributed trace shows your service finishing in 200ms, but there's a mysterious 500ms gap before the next service in the trace. How would you investigate?

title: Should this be one service or two?
prompt: A teammate proposes splitting the User service into a UserAuth service and a UserProfile service. Both currently live in one deployable that talks to one database. What questions would you ask, and what factors would lead you toward yes or no?

title: Choosing between strong and eventual consistency
prompt: You're building a 'likes' feature for a social network. When a user likes a post, the like count updates. Two requirements: counts shouldn't double-count if the user clicks twice, and the user should see their own like reflected immediately, but other users seeing it 5 seconds later is fine. Walk through your design choices.

title: Build vs buy for a search feature
prompt: Your product needs search across 10 million documents with filtering, highlighting, and typo tolerance. You're choosing between (a) Postgres full-text search, (b) self-hosted Elasticsearch, (c) managed Algolia. What questions would you ask before recommending one?

title: Why does your API timeout limit matter?
prompt: Your team has set a 30-second timeout on every internal HTTP call as a default. A senior engineer flags this as a problem. What's the concern, and how would you decide on the right values?

title: Designing a global API endpoint
prompt: Users in San Francisco, London, and Singapore all hit api.yourcompany.com. Your servers are in us-east. SF users see 80ms latency, London 120ms, Singapore 250ms. The 250ms is hurting conversion. What options do you have?

title: TLS connection storm at startup
prompt: You deploy a new version of a service that fans out to 200 backend instances on each request. After deploys, response times spike for 30 seconds and then settle. Investigation suggests TLS handshake overhead. How would you mitigate this?

title: Designing a 'follow' feature
prompt: A user can follow other users. The home page shows posts from people they follow, in reverse chronological order. Walk through how you'd model the data and serve the feed for a user who follows 500 people.

title: Many-to-many with permissions
prompt: In a project-management tool, a user can be a member of many projects, each with a role (owner/editor/viewer). Some queries: 'list all projects this user can edit', 'list all editors of this project', 'check if user X can edit project Y'. Design the schema and indexes.

title: Modeling a chat system
prompt: Design the data model for a 1-on-1 chat feature in a mobile app: messages, read receipts, typing indicators, message edits, and the list of recent conversations sorted by latest activity. Optimize for the read patterns: opening the conversation list, opening a specific conversation, sending a message.

title: Storing user uploads
prompt: Your app lets users upload profile photos (max 5MB each) and PDFs (max 50MB). Currently you base64-encode them and store them in a Postgres column. Things are getting slow. What would you change?

title: Background jobs vs cron
prompt: Your team currently runs 30 cron jobs across 3 servers. Some are critical (nightly billing); some are best-effort (cleanup tasks). When a server is replaced, jobs sometimes don't migrate. How would you redesign job scheduling?

title: Webhook delivery to flaky receivers
prompt: Your platform sends webhooks to customer-provided URLs on every order event. Some customer endpoints are slow (5+ seconds), some are down half the time, and a few have stopped responding entirely. Currently webhook failures are blocking the order flow. Design a more robust delivery system.

title: Designing a pub-sub system
prompt: Many services in your company want to react to 'order placed' events: inventory, billing, fulfillment, analytics, fraud detection. Today, the order service makes 5 HTTP calls. Design a pub-sub architecture and explain what changes for new subscribers.

title: GDPR right-to-be-forgotten
prompt: A user requests full deletion of their data under GDPR. Their data lives in: production database, daily backups (kept 90 days), an analytics warehouse, search index, and event logs. How would you handle the request technically and what's the correct policy?

title: Idempotent payment endpoint
prompt: Your /charge endpoint accepts a payment. The mobile client occasionally retries on flaky connections. You must NEVER charge a customer twice. Design the API contract and server-side handling.

title: Pagination at scale
prompt: Your /search endpoint uses LIMIT/OFFSET pagination. As pages get deeper (page 100, 200, 500) the query gets slower and the API timeouts more often. Why, and what's the fix?

title: Search-as-you-type
prompt: Build a search box that returns results as the user types, latency under 100ms, supporting 10,000 concurrent users on your platform. The dataset is 1 million products. Walk through the architecture.

title: Zero-downtime deployment
prompt: Your team deploys 5 times a day. Today, every deploy causes a 30-second outage as old instances drain and new ones come up. Walk through how you'd achieve zero-downtime deploys.

title: Database connection pool exhaustion
prompt: During a traffic spike, your service starts returning 500s. Logs show 'connection pool exhausted' errors. The pool size is 20. Each request holds a connection for the full request lifetime. Walk through your investigation and potential fixes.

title: Designing API versioning
prompt: You're shipping the first public version of your API. Customers will integrate against it and you need to evolve it without breaking them. What versioning strategy would you choose, and how would you handle deprecation?

title: Tracing slow requests
prompt: Users report that occasionally a page takes 10 seconds to load. The 99th percentile of your service's response time is 200ms, but the 99.9th percentile is 8 seconds. How would you investigate the long tail?

title: Choosing sync vs async API
prompt: A new endpoint generates a PDF report from large datasets — typically 5-30 seconds. The current implementation is synchronous and times out behind your 10-second proxy limit. What patterns do you have for fixing this?

title: Handling timezones in a global app
prompt: Your booking app shows appointment times to users worldwide. Bug reports keep coming in: 'my 3 PM appointment shows as 4 PM!', 'the date is wrong by a day after midnight!' Walk through what's likely going wrong and how you'd fix it.

title: Background data migration
prompt: You're consolidating two columns ('first_name' and 'last_name') into one ('full_name') on a 100M-row table. Production traffic is constant. The app code already supports both formats during the migration. How do you safely run the migration?

title: Detecting and mitigating a DDoS
prompt: Your origin server's CPU just hit 100% and customers report slowness. Logs show 5 IPs are sending 50,000 requests/minute each — far above normal. What immediate steps do you take, and how do you prevent recurrence?

title: Designing for graceful degradation
prompt: Your e-commerce homepage shows: hero banner, recommendations (powered by ML service), inventory status, reviews summary. The recommendations service has a 1% error rate. When it fails, the entire homepage 500s. How would you design for partial failure?

title: Exporting 1 GB of data to a user
prompt: A user requests an export of all their data. The export is 1 GB. Your API has a 30-second timeout and a 100 MB response size limit. How do you fulfill the request?
